sectionHeadings: 114: One gate definition, and it holds on a code-free corpus
1.1 The kit's own gate refuses the kit's own corpus
1.2 The refusal is correct, and its placement is not
1.3 The kit defines its gate three times, and the three disagree
1.4 The two definitions disagree about coupling as well, in opposite directions
3.1 `gate` reaches exit 0 on a corpus with no code
3.2 The ownership assertion is conditional, and the skip is announced
3.3 The gate takes a PR body and an explicit coupling control
3.4 The shipped workflow calls the target from both legs
3.6 Filing this spec moves spec 077's acceptance before the fix exists
record.summary: `make gate` exits 1 on the repository `spec-spine init --with-kit` has just created. The refusal is spec 059's, which made `index coverage --fail-on-untraced` refuse an empty coverage universe rather than pass it vacuously, and that is the right answer for a CI step named for the ownership assertion and the wrong one for the composite gate a specify-first adopter runs from minute one. `kit/AGENTS.md` already states the condition, as a commented line; `kit/Makefile` runs the assertion unguarded and `kit/govern.yml`'s pull-request leg restates the whole chain a third time, in a file whose own header says the gate has one definition rather than two that drift. This spec gives the gate one definition, gives it an announced skip rather than a silent one, gives it explicit controls for the two steps a caller may legitimately not want, and makes the shipped workflow call it from both legs.
record.title: One gate definition, and it holds on a code-free corpus
